newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker but well supported.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker but well supported.

text.p: London's October white sugar contract managed to hold on to nearby support at $326 as the market consolidated after last week's rally, traders said on Tuesday.
Light commission house buying of October kept the contract propped up, with the strength partially offset by trade against actuals selling.
"They look like they might be trying to push the market up a little...but I don't expect too much to happen in London this morning," said one trader.
"After the rally on Friday and an inside day yesterday, we're all waiting to see what happens."
A burst of fund buying in October raws on Friday gave London's equivalent whites contract a kick higher as the position regained most of the ground lost this month.
But on Tuesday activity was generally subdued and volume amounted to just 318 lots by 1120 GMT, concentrated in October.
October and December were both down by 20 cents, at $326.20 and $323.50 respectively.
Technical analysts said the fact that October had so far held support reflected the consolidation expected after such a strong push higher.
A test of October's life-high at $331.00 could now be expected in coming sessions, they said.
In physical news, India was reported to have been buyers at the end of last week of up to four cargoes of lesser-quality 100 ICUMSA sugar.
Iraq has offered to buy white sugar as part of the U.N.-sponsored oil-for-food deal at $379.50 per tonne c&f Umm Qasr or $420 c&f Baghdad, market sources said.
Just 35 lots were posted on the board on the Paris market. October was down 30 cents at $325.70 and December unchanged at $323.50. Nothing was traded on Matif's 100 ICUMSA white sugar market.
